# Medicina no convencional, otra alternativa para atender la salud de las mascotas

Natural Freshly lleva 32 años en el mercado como líder en productos naturales para consumo humano y ahora ha creado una línea exclusiva para mascotas Pets & Cats a base de recursos naturales.

Image: Analista LR Image: Analista LR

Ximena González

09 de octubre de 2019

Image: Natural Freshly Natural Freshly

En pleno siglo XXI las mascotas se han convertido no solo en una compañía sino en un miembro vital de la familia. Gatos, perros, pequeños roedores, aves, entre otras especies han integrado las familias y con ellos han venido apareciendo un sin número de problemas médicos, comportamentales y de adaptación. Por ello la medicina no convencional basada en los productos nutraceúticos donde su base es la mezcla de materias primas no químicas, brindan una excelente opción para las mascotas, minimizando efectos secundarios, prolongando su bienestar.

Laboratorios Natural Freshly lleva 32 años en el mercado como líder en productos naturales para consumo humano y ahora ha creado una línea exclusiva para mascotas Pets & Cats a base de recursos naturales donde se pueden tratar patologías comunes, trastornos comportamentales o simplemente prevenir y aliviar una dolencia.

Esta amplia línea brinda medicamentos como Vitacrunch compuestos de ingredientes naturales que estabilizan y alivian afecciones como alergias, gastritis, sobrepeso, trastornos articulares, trastornos urinarios y de defensas; además esencias florales que ayudan a manejar comportamientos inapropiados como miedo, agresividad, alergias, duelo, entre otras.

Por otro lado, hay algunos suplementos que aportan a las deficiencias orgánicas de las mascotas buscando su bienestar. Vale destacar que los resultados reportados y evidenciados en la administración de estos productos a base de recursos naturales han logrado abrir un gran campo en el área de medicina veterinaria y en todo lo relacionado con prevención.

Evaluacion de un producto a base de aceite esencial de oregano sobre la integridad intestinal, la capacidad de absorcion de nutrientes y el comportamiento productivo de pollos de carne (https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03728)
citeturn302academia7 [wordlim: 200] Published: 4.6 years ago; 
Title: Evaluacion de un producto a base de aceite esencial de oregano sobre la integridad intestinal, la capacidad de absorcion de nutrientes y el comportamiento productivo de pollos de carne
Authors: Diego Martinez
Date: Thu Apr  7 20:42:43 2022

Eight experiments were conducted to test an oregano-essential-oil-based product (PRO) on performance, gut health, and nutrient absorption capacity in broilers. The first three, up to 14d and without specific challenges, tested the effects on intestinal histology, skeletal integrity, and growth. Other two experiments, up to 28d birds were challenged to induce feed passage syndrome (STR) and test the effect on the antioxidant status and performance, contrasting later the results under a natural challenge in commercial conditions. Finally, in two other experiments, up to 21 d, birds challenged with coccidia were tested to determine the effects on coccidiosis, nutrient digestibility, and feed efficiency (FCR). Corn-soybean-fish meal diets were used. Under healthy conditions, PRO effects were observed on intestinal villus height and surface area, mucosa density and structure, villus to crypt ratio, goblet cells density, mucus production, body weight gain, and FCR (P<0.04), and carcass yield and bone density (P<0.08). Birds affected by STR showed effects (P<0.05) on superoxide dismutase activity, bodyweight gain, FCRE, non-normal feces frequency, bursal diameter, and dysbacteriosis. Birds affected by coccidia showed effects on cocci-positive ratio, cocci microscopic score, oocysts count, bursal diameter, body weight gain, FCR, apparent digestibility of dry matter and crude protein, protein and energy efficiencies (P<0.01), and nitrogen apparent retention (P<0.07). Results showed PRO added value to the diet favoring feed efficiency and performance.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Natural fumigation as a mechanism for volatile transport between flower organs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.13270)
citeturn302academia8 [wordlim: 200] Published: 2.1 years ago; 
Title: Natural fumigation as a mechanism for volatile transport between flower organs
Authors: Benoît Boachon, Joseph Lynch, Shaunak Ray, Jing Yuan, Kristian Mark P. Caldo, Robert Junker, Sharon A. Kessler, John A. Morgan, Natalia Dudareva
Date: Fri Sep 20 07:01:09 2024

Plants synthesize volatile organic compounds (VOCs) to attract pollinators and beneficial microorganisms, to defend themselves against herbivores and pathogens and for plant-plant communication. Generally, accumulation and emission of VOCs occur from the tissue of their biosynthesis. However, using biochemical and reverse genetic approaches, we demonstrate a new physiological phenomenon: inter-organ aerial transport of VOCs via natural fumigation. Before petunia flowers open, a tube-specific terpene synthase produces sesquiterpenes, which are released inside the buds and then accumulate in the stigma, potentially defending the developing stigma from pathogens. These VOCs also affect reproductive organ development and seed yield, which is a previously unknown function for terpenoid compounds. could serve as a mechanism to coordinate the timing of pistil development with petal development in order to insure that the stigma is receptive when the flowers are most likely to attract pollinators. Further studies are required to assess whether natural fumigation is conserved in flowering plants, to uncover the mechanisms involved, and to determine its evolutionary advantage in plant reproduction.
